summary: Opaque 429s after enabling client-side OAuth refresh + edge health probes
description:
Issue summary:
CartoMaps started seeing intermittent 429 responses for a production route shortly after enabling a client-side OAuth refresh workflow that fetches ephemeral API tokens on a per-request basis and after turning on more frequent edge health checks via their CDN (5s interval). Errors appear opaque (no retry-after header) and affect interactive map tile annotation UX.

Impact:
- ~0.8% request error rate to /v1/generate on peak minutes, user sessions experience failing requests in the map UI.
- Customer reports spike coincident with batch ingestion windows and automated health probes.

Environment:
- Customer tier: enterprise on dedicated pool
- Region: prod us-east (us-east-1)
- Route: /v1/generate (chat/completions)
- Client: custom JS SDK using OAuth refresh to exchange short-lived tokens per API call

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Enable short-lived token flow (refresh token endpoint returns 10s TTL tokens).
2) Configure CDN edge to run health probes against /healthz/ping every 5s from pooled IPs.
3) Observe 429s in application telemetry and in Redwood gateway logs.

Observed headers/log snippet (sanitized):
- Request-ID: req-0a7c9d
- x-rate-limit-status: missing
- Response: 429 with empty body and no Retry-After header in ~40% of 429s

Customer hypothesis:
They believe CDN health checks + per-request ephemeral-token refresh creates many unique API key signatures at the edge, which may be causing duplicated token accounting or misattribution to per-route refill windows. They ask how to isolate health-check traffic, whether short-lived tokens count against tenant quota differently, and recommended config for dedicated pools to avoid disrupting interactive users.

Attachments provided by customer:
- truncated local SDK trace (included)

investigation_notes: Checked gateway logs between 2026-03-10T08:00 and 2026-03-10T09:00 for tenant cartomaps-prod: saw 1.2k unique API token fingerprints originating from 8 CDN IPs; normal client traffic shows <20 unique fingerprints/min.

Verified rate-limiter behavior: per-key token bucket is computed before route-grouping; ephemeral keys created per-request bypass expected per-session smoothing, causing rapid drain of per-route burst pools.

Observed missing x-rate-limit-* headers on several 429s: root cause traced to short-circuit path in edge-proxy when token freshness check fails and early-reject path doesn't attach headers. Logged as bug in rate-limiter (PR linked).

Cross-referenced dedicated-pool metrics: autoscaler did not trigger; errors were throttle responses at gateway layer, not GPU queue saturation. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pool/dedicated-123/overview
SRE reproduced locally by running a small harness that minted new ephemeral tokens for each request and hit same route with 10qps from 8 IPs; reproduced opaque 429s and missing headers.
resolution_summary:
Short-term workaround applied: customer routed CDN health-checks to /internal-health and we whitelisted the CDN IPs (edge allowlist) so probes are excluded from tenant quota accounting. Recommended client change: cache/ reuse ephemeral tokens for short sessions (10s TTL tokens should be reused for multiple requests rather than refreshed per-request).

Planned permanent fix: INT-4312 will add a probe-exempt flag to the edge-proxy and a smoothing tweak to the rate-limiter to ensure very short-lived keys are aggregated onto the parent tenant refill window. A small reserved burst bucket for dedicated pools is proposed to keep health-checks from impacting interactive traffic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/2123 (in review).
postmortem_followups: Create runbook entry for customers deploying CDN health probes: recommend dedicated health route + single static key or IP allowlist. (owner: Support, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Add guard in edge-proxy to always include x-rate-limit headers on 4xx/5xx responses. (owner: SRE, linked INT-4312)
Implement aggregation of sub-minute ephemeral-token fingerprints to parent tenant accounting to prevent per-request key explosion. (owner: Infra, PR #2123)
Document best-practice for ephemeral-token usage in JS SDKs: reuse token per short-lived session and include jitter for refresh windows. (owner: DevRel)
Notify customer when INT-4312 lands and schedule a brief configuration review call.
